name: Zadun, a Ritz-Carlton Reserve
positioning: Ritz-Carlton Reserve resort (officially Zadún Los Cabos) overlooking the Sea of Cortez in Puerto Los Cabos, with suites and residences that have plunge pools
best_for: Travelers who want a quiet, private resort with personal service rather than Cabo San Lucas nightlife

facts.text: Zadún sits in Puerto Los Cabos, a quiet enclave near San José del Cabo.
Most guest rooms, suites, villa and residences face the Sea of Cortez, with terraces and private plunge pools.
El Barrio serves Mexican breakfasts and street-food-inspired lunches.
Equis has an omakase-style raw bar.
The resort's three nine-hole golf courses overlook the Sea of Cortez and were designed by Greg Norman and Jack Nicklaus.
The property uses renewable energy sources and has electric vehicle charging stations and electric golf carts.
The majority of the resort meets ADA standards with ramps and wheelchair-friendly pathways.
The multi-bedroom residences give children space, and the resort runs activities through the Ritz-Carlton Ambassadors of the Environment program.

highlights.text: Zadún is part of Ritz-Carlton's Reserve collection, whose properties are meant to feel like private estates, and guests are assigned personal tosoani (dream keepers).
Accommodations are suites and full residences, all with plunge pools and butler service.
Sensei is a 29,000-square-foot spa devoted to multisensory journeys.
Whales are visible from guest rooms during migration season.
The Candil bar is in the resort's lighthouse and has an agave program, with a signature Desert Moon cocktail of mezcal, prickly pear and a hint of chili.

considerations.text: The beach at Zadún is not swimmable because of a steep drop-off and strong currents.
The resort is in a quiet enclave near San José del Cabo, away from Cabo San Lucas' more party-centric scene.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the ultra-luxury positioning.
